  • Chi ha giocato meno ha dato delle risposte?

In a recent development, la Juventus parte piano, 'si incasina', come ammesso dallo stesso Spalletti, ma poi ha ragione dell'Omonia in virtù di una reazione di pancia e di una superiorità tecniche che si concretizza in modo evidente nella ripresa. Dopo lo shock del gol iniziale di Satka, su errore di Neto, la Juve reagisce col gran gol di Cambiaso e il 2-1 di Ekhator, che fa esultare l'Allianz Stadium dopo un inizio di mugugni. Nella ripresa sale in cattedra la qualità, con Conceicao e Boga che confezionano il poker finale. Con questo successo la Juve sale al secondo posto della classifica di Europa League, in posizione privilegiata per il passaggio del turno.

Industry observers note that luciano Spalletti ha parlato così dopo il successo interno contro l'Omonia ai microfoni di Sky Sport, esaltando la prova dei bianconeri: "All'inizio abbiamo commesso un paio di incertezze che gli altri hanno sfruttato, naturalmente così si incasina la capacità di esibire le tue cose. Poi Cambiaso ha rimesso le cose a posto con questo grande gol, dopo la squadra ha giocato più tranquilla".

Chi ha giocato meno ha dato delle risposte? "Sì, non è facile trovare subito la condizione, alcuni giocatori mancavano da un po' di tempo. Per festeggiare il Natale, quest'anno la Lazio ha pensato ad un evento differente rispetto alla consueta cena, che si svolgeva di solito a Spazio Novecento.

CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM.

Recent findings suggest that come si legge dal comunicato della Lazio con la lettera di Lotito riportata dal Corriere dello Sport, quest'anno l'invito per i tesserati della Lazio è per sabato 19 dicembre alle 15.00 per celebrare la messa di Natale. Inoltre verranno destinate risorse al sostegno di alcune realtà della nostra città che ogni giorno si impegnano ad aiutare le persone e le famiglie che vivono situazioni di difficoltà”.

A tutti i tesserati, dipendenti e collaboratori della S.S. Lazio.

il Natale è soprattutto un momento per stare insieme, ritrovarsi e ricordare ciò che conta davvero.

Quest’anno abbiamo pensato di scambiarci gli auguri in un modo diverso, più semplice, ma forse proprio per questo ancora più significativo.

Sabato 19 dicembre 2026, alle ore 15:00, ci ritroveremo nella parrocchia San Tommaso Moro, di Don Gabriele, nel quartiere San Lorenzo a Roma, per celebrare insieme la Santa Messa di Natale. Vorrei che fosse un momento per tutti noi, per sentirci parte di una comunità che ogni giorno condivide lavoro, impegno, responsabilità, gioie e difficoltà. Perché la Lazio, prima ancora di essere una società sportiva, è fatta di persone.

Quest’anno abbiamo anche deciso di vivere lo spirito del Natale attraverso un gesto concreto di solidarietà, destinando risorse al sostegno di alcune realtà della nostra città che ogni giorno si impegnano ad aiutare le persone e le famiglie che vivono situazioni di difficoltà.

Ci sono tante persone e tante famiglie che stanno attraversando momenti complicati. Credo che il modo migliore per vivere lo spirito del Natale sia anche quello di pensare a loro, rinunciando a qualcosa per noi per poter offrire qualcosa agli altri.

Non sarà un gesto che risolverà tutti i problemi, ma sarà il nostro modo di esserci, concretamente.

Mi piacerebbe davvero che il 19 dicembre fossimo tutti presenti. Non per un appuntamento formale, ma per il piacere di ritrovarci, guardarci negli occhi, scambiarci gli auguri e condividere un momento che appartiene a tutti noi.

Perché essere una comunità significa anche questo: sentirsi parte di qualcosa e sapere che, insieme, possiamo fare del bene.

Vi aspetto e, fin da ora, auguro a voi e alle vostre famiglie un Natale sereno, con l’auspicio che il nuovo anno possa portare salute, pace e soddisfazioni.

Claudio Lotito Presidente S.S. Lazio.

Parrocchia San Tommaso Moro Via dei Ramni, 40, 00185 Roma (angolo Via dei Marrucini).

#142588. Tech Report: Gary Neville tears into Man United's Matthijs de Ligt for 'unforgivable' defending that led to Leny Yoro's red card - and claims duo played like 'they have never had basic defensive training'

Tech Report: Gary Neville tears into Man United's Matthijs de Ligt for 'unforgivable' defending that led to Leny Yoro's red card - and claims duo played like 'they have never had basic defensive training'

📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (775 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dailymail

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 12:23 EST, 22 November 2026 | Updated: 10:28 EST, 24 November 2026.
  • Gary Neville led the criticism of Manchester United's defending in the opening minutes against Liverpool as Mauricio Pochettino's reign started in disastrous fashion at Anfield.
  • After just eight minutes, his plans were thrown into tatters when errors from Matthijs de Ligt and Leny Yoro saw the latter sent off before Liverpool took a swift lead.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By LEWIS BROWNING, SPORTS REPORTER.

Published: 12:23 EST, 22 November 2026 | Updated: 10:28 EST, 24 November 2026.

Gary Neville led the criticism of Manchester United's defending in the opening minutes against Liverpool as Mauricio Pochettino's reign started in disastrous fashion at Anfield.

After just eight minutes, his plans were thrown into tatters when errors from Matthijs de Ligt and Leny Yoro saw the latter sent off before Liverpool took a swift lead.

A long ball from Ronald Araujo should have been dealt with easily by De Ligt, but the Dutchman found himself in no man's land, left the ball, and Alexander Isak raced clear.

That left Yoro scrambling to try to recover the situation for his side, but Isak stepped across him and he ended up fouling the Reds forward.

Referee Sam Barrott wasted no time in pulling out the red card, and United found themselves reduced to 10 men just minutes into a vital clash.

And former United defender Neville didn't hold back when it came to his analysis as he tore into the two players at fault.

According to recent reports, leny Yoro is SENT OFF after eight minutes! 😱 pic.twitter.com/VKYvckvBBP.

Gary Neville torn into Manchester United duo Leny Yoro (right) and Matthijs de Ligt after the former was sent off.

Neville (pictured) questioned why the duo were playing as if they had 'never had basic training of how to play in defence'.

'When I saw De Ligt's name on the team sheet I have to admit I was absolutely stunned,' he said, speaking on Sky Sports. 'And the reason I was stunned was because of this. If you'd watched him in Como four weeks ago he was very much well off it and that is just a basic ball over the top.

It has been revealed that 'It's his problem to start with, Yoro can be further across, but De Ligt is miles away from it, then Yoro has to get further round, he reacts late, his anticipation is poor. It's so clumsy from Yoro, he makes a lot of these types of mistakes.

'You could argue Isak delays to make sure Yoro runs into him, but it's naivety.'.

Pochettino was left scrambling to think of ideas to tighten up the defence but, before he could bring Harry Maguire on, it was 2-0 through Florian Wirtz.

Maguire eventually came on but it felt like too little, too late.

'We saw him in Como and he has been out for a year,' Neville continued on De Ligt. 'It is really tough to come back. To have him out there in a game like this, he has been exposed. Yoro's positioning is poor, he has to be across, you have to cover your mate. It is bad all around from United.

'Michael Carrick will be watching and say that's what I was having to deal with.'.

And his criticism didn't stop there. After having the chance to re-watch the incident, Neville's criticism grew even stronger.

De Ligt (left) failed to deal with a long ball as Alexander Isak (right) raced away before the foul.

Former United captain Roy Keane (pictured) added that he was 'amazed' by the errors made.

Industry observers note that 'It's as bad defending from two centre backs defending a long ball as you will see,' the former defender, who likened a return from a year out to playing after six pints of alcohol, added. 'De Ligt is well out of it - he's been out so I have some sympathy. But between them, to let the ball beat you, it's unforgivable.

'It is shocking. Whilst Man United have those types of defenders in their team, they have no chance of keeping a clean sheet.

In a recent development, 'It's basic understanding of how to play a position. It's the fundamentals. It's like these guys have never had basic training of how to play in defence.'.

Former United captain Roy Keane chimed in too, adding at half-time: 'It doesn't matter if it's a back four or back five, you do the basics right.

Sources indicate that 'I'm amazed at this level, I know he's been out a while, but it's really poor defending. He's never getting that ball.

'If you're a defender you always expect the worst. Isak's done well and I actually don't think he's going to get the ball.

'There's no way he's (Yoro) getting the ball, it's clumsy by United. Straight ball over the top and he's in big trouble. But there's no way he's getting that ball. I know he's quick and sharp but it's really poor defending. Players not smelling danger.'.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In casa Napoli si lavora al mercato e la priorità è regalare ad Allegri un vice-Hojlund, un calciatore che possa dare ricambio in maniera consistente al danese e allo stesso tempo eventualmente giocare insieme.

Sources indicate that il club sembra intenzionato a puntare sull’attaccante campano Sebastiano Esposito, attualmente in prestito al Sassuolo, ma di proprietà del Cagliari. Il calciatore è il profilo adatto, per caratteristiche e cifre, per sostituire Lorenzo Lucca, sempre più ai margini e ormai giocatore che verrà ceduto a gennaio. La trattativa tra le parti è già cominciata e il Napoli sembra intenzionato a sferrare a gennaio l’attacco decisivo per Esposito.

Come riporta Il Mattino il Napoli è in pole per Sebastiano Esposito, nelle ultime settimane l’agente del giocatore Giuffredi ha incontrato Giovanni Manna e la trattativa è stata ormai già preimpostata. Il presidente azzurro De Laurentiis vuole riportare l’attaccante in Campania e il giocatore può arrivare a costi piuttosto contenuti per un profilo da Nazionale.

Il Sassuolo può riscattare Esposito per 10 milioni di euro circa e il Napoli potrebbe chiudere la trattativa a circa 14-15 milioni di euro, una trattativa che il Napoli potrebbe realizzare anche in prestito con obbligo di riscatto a fine anno. Le parti ragionano sul da farsi, ma sarà Esposito il nuovo attaccante per gennaio.

For decades, most countries have followed the same model of biomedical innovation. Basic research is undertaken mostly by universities and academia, and private industry leads the translation of research into health solutions1.

This approach has generated extraordinary drugs and therapies as well as economic success. In 2022, the pharmaceutical sector contributed US$2.3 trillion — or around 1.7% — to global gross domestic product (GDP) and supported 75 million jobs2.

How tech billionaires are disrupting biomedical science.

How tech billionaires are disrupting biomedical science.

However, market failures have been common. Companies have underinvested in developing therapeutics for common diseases with poorly understood biological mechanisms, such as depression, anxiety and kidney disease, because they consider them too commercially risky or unprofitable to pursue3.

To address this gap, we propose an adapted innovation model based on mission-driven public–private partnerships (PPPs), in which government acts as a leading strategic investor. By bringing together the best scientists in academia and industry and lowering risks in industry development in areas of public need and for diseases with limited understanding, this model would accelerate translation, advance health and increase economic returns.

Sources indicate that here, we outline how it would work. It will require systems to ensure affordable access to drugs and therapies, as well as revenue sharing between public and private partners to guarantee public benefits and to support investments in innovation.

Recent findings suggest that complex diseases that affect swathes of the population create persistent health and economic burdens. Yet, the current biomedical innovation model has proved limited in addressing evolving health needs. Because private investment is guided by assessments of risk and return, it tends to favour diseases with well-defined biological mechanisms and high commercial potential. Diseases that are biologically complex, varied or associated with uncertain markets remain underexplored.

According to recent reports, for example, in 2023, more than 300 million people globally had depression. The condition will cost the global economy an estimated $12 trillion between 2025 and 20504. In the United States in 2024, one in five people reported that they had received a diagnosis of major depressive disorder during their lifetime, resulting in an economic burden of $334 billion annually across health-care, household-related and workforce costs5. Yet, the leading drug class for depression (selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors) has remained unchanged since the 1970s6.

The grand blueprint to transform psychiatry — by personalizing mental-health care.

The grand plan to transform psychiatry — by personalizing mental-health care.

Other chronic diseases impose similarly large burdens. For example, chronic kidney disease affects around 800 million people worldwide — nearly one in seven — and is projected to become the fifth leading cause of death globally by 2040 if current trends continue7,8. Yet, existing therapies cannot stem its toll on human lives.

Antimicrobial resistance is another example, which is associated with 4.7 million deaths globally each year and could contribute to 10 million deaths annually by 2050. Increased treatment costs for people with resistant infections amount to $1 trillion every year9. The antibiotic development pipeline has been depleted over time as economic factors render companies’ return on investment lower than that for other drug classes9. These factors include insufficient funding for research and challenging business models, given the short duration of antibiotic treatments and the need to reserve successful new antibiotics as drugs of last resort, to be used after all other options have failed.

Sources indicate that bringing a therapy to market from discovery can take 10–15 years and cost anywhere between $880 million and $2.3 billion10,11. The majority (90%) of drug candidates fail after entering clinical studies, clinical trials and drug-approval processes12. And companies won’t invest if they are unsure whether a drug will be profitable.

Consequently, many diseases and conditions have no or few available therapies or only modestly effective options13. What’s needed is a mission-driven strategy to guide scientific capabilities and industry development towards areas of public need by elucidating biological mechanisms and aligning incentives for diseases in which market forces alone are insufficient14.

In a recent development, we propose addressing this misalignment of incentives by reconceptualizing the government’s role in therapeutic advancement through a model of mission-driven PPP. Complementing existing grant-based systems, the model would position the government as a principal investor in select areas of therapeutic development.

The government would thus influence which areas of health and science receive concentrated attention and how successful outcomes are deployed for the public good. Such a model could address specific national needs and global challenges. Here are seven components.

Technicians at work in a pharmaceutical factory.Credit: Getty.

Select disease targets. We propose the establishment of a government-appointed independent advisory body or commission tasked with identifying priority disease targets using transparent, evidence-based criteria, including disease burden, economic cost, scientific readiness and demonstrable market failure. Further criteria to gauge and consider public input into the selection process could be implemented to ensure public trust.

In a recent development, set up collaborations. A national government, acting alone or as part of an international consortium, would assume a leading role in supporting basic research into biological mechanisms. It would do so by bringing together basic scientists from academia and translational experts from industry to reduce risks in translational development. Private industry would contribute expertise in drug development, clinical trials, regulatory strategy, manufacturing and commercialization.

It has been revealed that provide initial investments. The proposed PPP would not replace existing grant-based systems or market-driven innovation; rather, it would act as a complement by targeting disease areas in which market risks and incentives consistently fail to generate sufficient private investment. The approach could yield fresh therapies and reduce the cost of care to society while generating revenue from latest products.

Could measuring immune health reshape medical care?

Could measuring immune health reshape medical care?

Sources indicate that in the United States, we propose a federal investment of one billion dollars annually over ten years, directed to specific disease areas. That is less than 1.8% of total US government spending on biomedical research, which was $54.5 billion in 2024. This would be supplemented by smaller investments of 10–20% of one billion dollars from a consortium of philanthropic foundations and industry partners joining the initiative in response to a request for application. Given the high costs of bringing a new drug to market, a $10-billion total investment should provide the scale and time needed to pursue about three major disease targets10–12.

It has been revealed that feed revenues back in. Public return is a defining feature of the PPP. Existing biomedical funding structures are mainly grant making, with the implication that public benefit will emerge indirectly through the downstream health improvements and economic growth spurred by discovery. By contrast, this PPP framework would directly incorporate public accountability as well as returns.

The government would need to leverage its status as a majority investor to ensure access, fair pricing and affordability. It might require conditions such as agreements to ensure access. Pricing frameworks could incorporate a value-based approach to pricing, in which health insurers offer reimbursements determined by a drug’s value for patients. Affordability conditions, such as reasonable-pricing clauses, would also serve as powerful leverage.

The 125th cap was no different to the first for Harry Kane, who has now been in the business of goal accumulation for so long that it is only at the landmark moments, that all of us are obliged to step back and take in the full scale of the work he has created.

Peter Shilton took 20 years to rack up his 125 caps, while for Kane it has been just 11 – and then there are the goals. Two more on Tuesday took him to 91 which means that only 12 other England players in history have more England caps than Kane has England goals. This unassuming man from Chingford, who looks like a mildly rebellious academic from the late 1950s, was at it again: the first-time strike, the back-post header. He has some misses across these 11 years, most infamously from the penalty spot against France at the Qatar World Cup almost four years ago, so, yes, there are some regrets too. But what sticks is the way he has taken his chances – again and again.

Following his debut goal in 2015 against Lithuania, Kane has missed just 27 of the 152 England games since. He has added to the total like a great Test batsman patiently moving the scoreboard along. There was a bad run without goals in 2020 and before that in 2018. He scored only five in his first 17 caps and then scored 14 in his next 10. Against a very mediocre Czech Republic team this was classic late-era Kane, picking his moments and taking those chances with the usual absence of nerves. He was even substituted before the end.

Afterwards at a Wembley press conference to mark the occasion, he invoked the cricket analogy himself on the question of scoring 100 England goals. “Being in the 90s, I try not to think about it too much, and it’s like I guess being a cricketer in the 90s. The more you think about the hundred… you don’t always get there.” There has still not been the elusive major trophy in the Kane England years but there has been success relative to the three decades that came before it. Semi-finals, finals – a good team if not a winning team.

Industry observers note that at the centre of it has been a man around whom there has never been any scandal or, by the usual measure, much that might be described as spectacular. Rather it has been the scope of Kane’s career that is the most striking. The volume of the goals, of appearances, the capacity to be available – to play, to score – and the absolute quality of the player himself. He is determined to wring the very last drop out of his talent and usually refuses to acknowledge the prospect of the end, although there was a nod to it this time. “At some stage you know this opportunity isn’t going to be here,” he said. “I’m not going to be around forever, and I still hope that’s a long way away. But ultimately, of course, there’s times you’re tired or you’re injured, but I know I’ll miss it when it’s done. I try to always remind myself that and always try to make myself available.”.

According to recent reports, one expects that when the end comes it will not be as rancorous as the final exit of Cristiano Ronaldo from Portugal, a drama playing out elsewhere. At some point, Kane will take his leave and it is likely to be as unassuming as the rest of it. He will be back at Wembley, injury permitting, for cap No 126 next month against Croatia. He talks like a different person to the one he was even five years ago – with a confidence and certainty about his place in the world. As opposed to the younger Kane, who seemed to regard everything outside his goalscoring tunnel vision with a general sense of bemusement.

According to recent reports, “Availability,” he noted, “is one of the biggest strengths you can have at this level for any coach.” He was keen to emphasise his “all-round leadership” too, “a lot of assets off the pitch”. He still measures himself in goals, of course, and perhaps there will be a Ballon d’Or too later this month – a prize that has eluded generations of England players before him who have won much more for their clubs than Kane has done. The good news for Kane is that his last England years will be spent in a very good England team – one which was on another level to its opposition on this occasion too.

Sources indicate that no team in the top tier of the Nations League has scored more goals than England – 14 in the last four match days. Tuchel’s name was sung at Wembley and even if the World Cup semi-final collapse in Atlanta in July has not been entirely forgotten, the roughest edges have been taken off somewhat. Another great performance from Jude Bellingham and also from Morgan Rogers, in place of Bukayo Saka. Another dominant Elliot Anderson performance in midfield. They left Wembley to applause and a sense of optimism renewed.

It has been revealed that england kept the ball with such authority, and none more so than Bellingham. Trent Alexander-Arnold came back at right-back. Myles Lewis-Skelly returned for another bite at a Wembley midfield job. As in Prague last week, there was a self-inflicted Czech calamity in the first half. The captain Vladimir Coufal appeared to lose his cool at the threat of the England attack all over the Czechs’ half. No other reason for this Premier League experienced full-back to fling himself at Kane’s cross and drill the ball past Newcastle goalkeeper Lukas Hornicek on 27 minutes.

According to recent reports, the second goal, on 40 minutes, was one for the ages. Anderson’s ball out to the right was met first time by Rogers for the cross and Kane ran into the space, as he has done so many times, to deliver a finish struck with customary assuredness. Bellingham almost flicked in Rogers’s cross on 56 minutes and from the corner that came after, Kane nodded in a header at the back post from Lewis Hall’s cross. All mentioned, the defending was woeful but there was nothing wrong with the finish.

Thomas Tuchel believes England have taken a step forward from their World Cup heartbreak over this international break and remarked he was “honoured” to hear fans sing his name.

England finished their four Nations League games with a 3-0 win over Czech Republic, in which Harry Kane scored twice on his record-equalling 125th appearance.

It meant that Tuchel’s team have won three and lost one, against Spain, of their four games since the World Cup, after which the England head coach was heavily criticised for the semi-final defeat to Argentina.

Tuchel seems to have won the forgiveness of some England supporters, who sang his name at the start and the end of Tuesday’s game.

Industry observers note that “It means a lot,” Tuchel noted. “It’s amazing to have a song. It’s the biggest honour. And I’m very happy and very honoured. They can be sure that I will give my absolute best to make our team win and play well.”.

Asked if he sensed a change in mood around his England team since the fall-out from the World Cup, Tuchel mentioned: “I do and I think it’s necessary to move on. I think I can only repeat that we didn’t go out in the group stage. Sometimes it feels like that and we didn’t. As I said, our aim was always to progress, move forward and improve.”.

Tuchel snapped back at a reporter who questioned why he felt it necessary to repeat that England had not gone out in the group stage of the World Cup, claiming the criticism had felt a “little bit” too harsh.

Industry observers note that but on whether England have shown they are a step ahead of where the team were at the World Cup during this international camp, Tuchel was far more positive and replied: “Of course and that’s what we have to do. That is our goal to constantly improve and develop.

“We had these experiences together and we had a major tournament together, and it was very positive. It’s necessary to move forward and improve, especially in sports. This is what we’re trying to do.

Industry observers note that “We adjusted some details in our structure and we didn’t compromise on the effort and the intensity, and on the togetherness of the team. The players who were with us in the World Cup took care of these standards and of the culture within the team, off the pitch and on the pitch, and I think that’s what you could see.”.

We played a very good match, very fluid and to put it into context it was the fourth match in 11 or 12 days. We dominated the whole match, had some good opportunities, scored some beautiful goals. Subs were strong. Very good performance again.

[Leading the way, Mr Kane] Of course. That’s what he does. I don’t take it for granted. It’s just exceptional, every single match. It’s just difficult to find newly introduced words to express it.

Training, attitude, cohesion, belief, of course [is why they’re stronger than ever].

According to recent reports, shilton’s took him 20 years as Gordon Banks was simply too good in the couple of years following his debut and then a couple of managers, Don Revie and Ron Greenwood, preferred Ray Clemence until the latter finally plumped for Shilton as No 1 in 1979. Kane’s, by contrast, have taken him 11. In that time he has been rested for a handful of friendlies but has not been unused in a competitive match when fit since Gareth Southgate left him out of the 5-0 victory over Sam Marino in 2021’s World Cup qualifier when Dominic Calvert-Lewin scored two and Ollie Watkins one goal on his debut.

In a recent development, england played the Czech Republic a week ago, winning 2-0 in Prague by virtue of Anthony Gordon’s cute header and Kane’s clever shot through a defender’s legs but they huffed and puffed for ages against a team harshly reduced to 10 men until they blew the house down. It has been revealed that in the past England have had problems backing up their best performances – the 4-1 evisceration of the Dutch at Euro 96 was followed by the cagey display in the quarter-final against Spain before prevailing on penalties, the 5-1 victory in Munich in 2001 led to a drab 2-0 win against Albania at St James’ Park the following Tuesday, in 2016 they went to Berlin and beat world champions Germany but were thumped by Netherlands, who had not even qualified for Euro 2016, a couple of days later. Even their thrilling, second-half showing against Croatia in their World Cup opener in June preceded the dreary 0-0 draw with Ghana.

Carlos Augusto ha rinnovato il proprio contratto con l’Inter. Il club nerazzurro ha infatti reso noto di aver raggiunto un accordo con il difensore brasiliano classe 1999, che sarà nerazzurro fino al 30 giugno 2031. “Inesauribile, solido, decisivo: difensore forte e veloce, esterno fisico e tecnico, minaccia costante nell’area avversaria. Carlos Augusto è diventato, nel corso degli anni, un elemento chiave nello scacchiere nerazzurro: la sua duttilità lo ha reso un giocatore fondamentale, capace di ricoprire nel migliore dei modi il ruolo di braccetto sinistro nella difesa a tre e quello di esterno a tutta fascia. Capacità con cui ha contribuito ai recenti successi dell’Inter, con cui è pronto a scrivere nuovi, entusiasmanti capitoli grazie al rinnovo di contratto che lo legherà al Club fino al 2031.

Il Venezia continua il percorso di consolidamento e raggiunge l'accordo con uno dei suoi punti di forza. A rinnovare il suo accordo con gli arancioneroverdi è stavolta Hainaut, diventato perno inamovibile dei lagunari. Di seguito il comunicato: "Il Venezia FC comunica di aver raggiunto un accordo per il rinnovo del contratto di Antoine Hainaut, che continuerà a vestire la maglia arancioneroverde fino al 30 giugno 2030. Arrivato in laguna nella stagione 2025/26, Hainaut, 24 anni, ha collezionato finora 52 presenze ufficiali con la maglia del Venezia FC, totalizzando 7 gol e 8 assist. Protagonista della promozione in Serie A nella stagione 2025/26, Antoine Hainaut ha condiviso con il Venezia FC un percorso di grande valore, affermandosi progressivamente come uno dei punti di riferimento della squadra".

Stringere i denti fino a gennaio, per poi intervenire sul mercato e rinforzare una rosa che sta facendo i conti con numerose assenze. È questa la strategia del Milan, alle prese con un'emergenza infortuni che condiziona le scelte di Amorim. Per questo la dirigenza rossonera sta già lavorando sottotraccia per allungare le rotazioni, individuando nella fascia sinistra una delle principali priorità. Il nome che stuzzica maggiormente l'interesse del Diavolo, scrive il Corriere dello Sport, è quello di Alejandro Balde. Il laterale spagnolo, classe 2003, potrebbe lasciare il Barcellona già nella finestra invernale e il suo agente Jorge Mendes sarebbe al lavoro per valutare le possibili opportunità. La valutazione dei blaugrana si aggira intorno ai 50 milioni di euro, mentre l'ingaggio del giocatore è di circa 5 milioni annui. A favorire l'operazione potrebbe essere lo scarso impiego del terzino, che finora ha collezionato appena tre presenze in campionato, senza mai completare una partita. Una situazione che non soddisfa le aspettative del giocatore e che potrebbe spingerlo a cercare maggiore spazio altrove. Il Milan starebbe valutando la formula del prestito oneroso con diritto di riscatto, eventualmente trasformabile in obbligo al verificarsi di determinate condizioni. La concorrenza, però, non manca visto che anche la Juventus, la Roma e diversi club stranieri seguono con attenzione l'evoluzione della situazione.

According to recent reports, juan Miranda ha probabilmente trovato in Raffaele Palladino l'allenatore capace più di tutti gli altri di esaltare le sue caratteristiche. Da quando il manager di Mugnano di Napoli s'è insediato a Casteldebole, il laterale spagnolo ha sfornato assist a raffica. Ben quattro decisivi nelle quattro sfide tra il 17 e il 31 ottobre. Miranda contro il Parma ha poi rimediato un infortunio al bicipite femorale della coscia sinistra, un infortunio che l'ha costretto a saltare la sfida contro l'Udinese e quasi certamente lo costringerà a saltare anche la prossima contro il Venezia. Nel frattempo però tiene banco la questione rinnovo di contratto. "Ci stiamo approcciando. Abbiamo parlato con i suoi agenti, vediamo come procede", ha dichiarato il direttore sportivo rossoblù Marco Di Vaio a margine della sfida contro l'Udinese su un nuovo accordo da raggiungere col laterale di Olivares che il Bologna ha ingaggiato a parametro zero nell'estate 2024. In quell'occasione, Miranda ha sottoscritto un contratto di tre anni col Bologna con opzione per la quarta stagione, un'opzione che il club emiliano ha già esercitato estendendo così il contratto fino al 30 giugno 2028. Ma cosa ci sarà nel suo futuro? Miranda a Bologna si trova bene e un rinnovo del contratto per una ulteriore stagione o fino al 2030 è una possibilità. Allo stesso tempo, diverse significant si stanno interessando a un giocatore che oggi è uno dei migliori laterali mancini della nostra Serie A. Sulle sue tracce soprattutto Milan e Juventus, due club che soprattutto in vista della prossima stagione cercano nuove garanzie per quella zona di campo. E Miranda lo sarebbe: lo confermano i numeri e le prestazioni di questa prima parte di stagione.

Nonostante le tante difficoltà riscontrate in questa prima parte di stagione nel ruolo al Milan di vice Goncalo Ramos, mezza Serie A continua ad avere i riflettori puntati sul baby talento Francesco Camarda. Blindato in estate da Amorim in rossonero, l'attaccante classe 2008 non si è dimostrato all'altezza di certi palcoscenici ed è per questo che la dirigenza sta studiando il giusto percorso per consentirgli una crescita ben diversa da quella vissuta a Lecce, dove Camarda si ritrovò immerso in uno degli ambienti più complessi per mettersi in mostra e guadagnare fiducia. Come detto, però, il Wonderkid di Via Aldo Rossi continua ad ad accrescere la lista degli estimatori, a cui si sarebbe aggiunto pure il Torino. Escluso Che Adams, il cui rendimento continua ad essere una costante, in casa granata l'inizio di questa stagione ha messo in luce una serie di evidenti problemi nel trovare la via del gol. Anche due pilastri come Simeone e Vlasic sembrano aver smarrito la brillantezza della scorsa stagione ed è per questo che il ds Petrachi, molto attento nella valorizzazione dei giovani italiani (vedasi gli acquisti dei vari Mascardi, Comuzzo e Fortini), avrebbe messo nel mirino, tra gli altri, proprio Francesco Camarda. Dalla loro parte i granata hanno un importante asso nella manica da potersi giocare, visto che al Filadelfia Camarda ritroverebbe Ignazio Abate. Fu quest'ultimo a lanciarlo nel 2023, a soli 15 anni, in Primavera, dove il 2008 si impose come uno degli attaccanti più interessanti del panorama giovanile italiano e non solo. La lista delle pretendenti però è lunga e se il Torino vorrà accaparrarselo dovrà battere una concorrenza feroce. In Serie A Camarda è finito anche sui taccuini di Udinese, Genoa, Cagliari - dove potrebbe essere legato a Paul Mendy, che piace al Milan -, oltre che a ad una serie di club esteri e di Serie B, Sampdoria su tutti.

Un pari casalingo contro il Brugge e due vittorie contro Viking e Sabah chiuderebbero il discorso e gli azzurri si garantirebbero i Playoff con la possibilità di andare agli Ottavi di finale.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Female mosquitoes use several sensory systems to locate a host whose blood they can feed on. One of these systems is a group of proteins known as ionotropic receptors, which detect the acidic compounds in human sweat that contribute to its sour smell. Writing in Nature, Xu et al.1 report 3D structures of an ionotropic-receptor complex from the malaria-spreading mosquito Anopheles stephensi. The structures show how the binding of an acid activates the receptor, which then opens its ion-conducting pore and generates an electrical signal that helps to guide the mosquito towards a human host.

Zitto zitto, Amorim sta cucinando un Milan da scudetto. Juve smarrita: è Milano-Roma sia in campo che nel Palazzo, tra i tormenti di Abete

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Il titolo era questo già prima della gara con l’Olympiacos, e forse sarebbe rimasto lo stesso anche se il Milan al Pireo avesse perso.
  • According to recent reports, E invece, Amorim sta cucinando un Milan che si può togliere belle soddisfazioni.
  • Non ha sogni, almeno per ora, neanche la Juventus.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Il titolo era questo già prima della gara con l’Olympiacos, e forse sarebbe rimasto lo stesso anche se il Milan al Pireo avesse perso. Che poi i rossoneri abbiano vinto, con una rimonta figlia dell’orgoglio ma prima ancora della loro qualità, va solo a corroborare una tesi. Zitto zitto, in realtà, Ruben Amorim non ci sta quasi mai. Dice tante cose, alcune delle quali all’apparenza con il principale scopo di stupire l’interlocutore. Il punto non è la sua silenziosità nelle conferenze stampa, quanto il fatto che, finora, al Milan non ci credesse davvero nessuno. Troppo americano Gerry Cardinale, troppo sui generis la - non - struttura dirigenziale immaginata in estate, troppo smargiasso quel suo allenatore, troppo cocenti le delusioni degli ultimi anni.

According to recent reports, E invece, Amorim sta cucinando un Milan che si può togliere belle soddisfazioni. Forse persino da scudetto, considerando che la distanza dalla vetta non è così ampia: cinque punti da una Lazio che chissà se davvero riuscirà a tenere questo ritmo da centometrista lungo tutta quella maratona che è un campionato di Serie A. Il Milan, piano piano, si sta ricompattando. Pecca ancora di solidità, ma in fin dei conti non ce l’hanno in molti in Italia, e nel frattempo sta trovando continuità. Inoltre, ha numeri, ha dribbling e gol in cantiere, pure quelli di Goncalo Ramos, che non è l’ultimo passante visto per caso in Via Aldo Rossi. Che Pulisic fosse il vero irrinunciabile tra lui e Leao era idea di molti: se ci si aggiungono schegge impazzite come Moreira - che giocatore - e Hutchinson, senza dimenticare Alphadjo Cisse, che per ora è l’unico milanista in doppia cifra, ecco che il povero Diavolo ha ritrovato una potenza di fuoco non così comune in Serie A e pure nell’Europa dei piccoli nella quale gli tocca correre attualmente. Se poi Cardinale dovesse (ri)aprire i cordoni della borsa a gennaio per l’Endrick di turno, allora i sogni di tricolore sarebbero ancora più legittimi, anche se resterebbero due dubbi: se non sarebbe meglio spendere per un difensore e se l’arrivo del brasiliano - o di chi per lui - non rischi di oscurare Cisse. Sarebbe un gran peccato.

Non ha sogni, almeno per ora, neanche la Juventus. Anche in questo caso il titolo era immaginato prima della partita di Europa League, e il fatto che i bianconeri abbiano avuto la meglio sull’Omonia, alla fine pure in bello stile, non cambia più di tanto lo stato dell’arte. Fa morale, per carità. Fa il paio con la vittoria sul Venezia, certo. Ma che siano serviti i cori dei tifosi per tirare fuori gli attributi - il tenore era quello, non c'è licenza poetica, al massimo edulcorazione - in una partita di Europa League già basta: con tutto il rispetto, la Juve “vera” l’Omonia non deve farlo nemmeno entrare in campo. Nessuno guarda con gli occhi del terrore la creatura di Luciano Spalletti, che si è smarrita prima dell’arrivo dell'allenatore toscano e non ha ancora ritrovato la retta via. Che poi Lucio, impegnato a lottare contro la sua squadra - non perché questa gli remi contro, non fraintendiamo: non ne ha l'identità per farlo - sottolinei come siano i giornalisti a chiedergli ogni volta di Vlahovic è curioso: è il segreto di Pulcinella che l’avrebbe tenuto volentieri e che vorrebbe un altro 9. Che poi abbia riscoperto il “target striker” dopo una carriera in cui non ci ha quasi mai puntato, questa è un’altra storia: l’allenatore che fece di Totti un meraviglioso centravanti s’è oggi scoperto bisognoso di un paracarro lì davanti. Ironie del pallone.

It has been revealed that la Juve, insomma, s’è smarrita perché velleità di scudetto non ne ha, e forse nemmeno di Champions League: chi cade dalla torre delle prime quattro, facciamo cinque se il ranking ci benedice? Ecco, appunto. Il tricolore quest’anno è storia di Roma contro Milano, nel senso di Lazio, Roma, Inter e Milan, nell’ordine in cui le mette la classifica. Chi ha di più è l’Inter, ma non è detto che vinca: al netto delle eventuali responsabilità di Chivu, in estate ha peggiorato in quasi ogni reparto, tolto l’attacco solo perché non l’ha toccato. È abbastanza particolare che lo sfondo a questa classifica sia un’altra sfida molto “Roma contro Milano” - è una banalizzazione, anche perché poi in Lombardia c’è chi vota per il primo e nel Lazio chi sceglie il secondo -, quella tra Giovanni Malagò e Adriano Galliani per la presidenza della Federcalcio, che vive le ultime battute, tra voli alti e colpi bassi. Anche qui, per la cronaca, la Juve, che un tempo decideva le sorti del calcio italiano, s’è persa e non s’è capito dove voglia andare a parare, nel tentativo di proteggere con l’inazione il posto in consiglio federale di Giorgio Chiellini, che probabilmente perderà comunque. Le ultime raccontano di un piccolo vantaggio dell’ex amministratore delegato del Milan, tutto da mettere alla prova dei colpi di scena da qui al 14 dicembre. Tra i due giganti dello sport, c’è un terzo che può risultare decisivo, e si chiama Giancarlo Abete.

Il presidente della Lega Nazionale Dilettanti ha in mano, almeno teoricamente, il 29% dei voti. Non è la percentuale della sua componente, ma quella dei voti che ha preso da candidato di bandiera lo scorso 22 giugno. Può darsi che sia un bottino leggermente ridimensionato nel tempo, ma è trasversale: la sua Lega varrebbe il 34%, ma non tutti lo seguirebbero se si schierasse, in compenso lo farebbero buone fette di Serie B (6%) e C (12%). Quale che sia il numero di preferenze che può davvero indirizzare - e questo è un tema, perché ciascun presidente di lega deve stare attento a non perdere la maggioranza interna, a costo di non schierarsi pur se vorrebbe -, è il più corteggiato perché si tratta di un pacchetto di voti che può decidere le elezioni: di sicuro sarebbe decisivo se appoggiasse Adriano Galliani, ma forse anche se si schierasse con Giovanni Malagò. Alla fine probabilmente non si schiererà, almeno non ufficialmente: perché mai rinunciare a questo ruolo di ago della bilancia fino all’ultimo secondo? Per di più, da indipendente, sarebbe il faro del consiglio federale dopo le elezioni: comunque vada a finire, l’organo sarà diviso e quasi ingestibile. Oltre a questi calcoli - e a quelli relativi alla durata del mandato: Galliani due anni, Malagò non punta certo a salutare nel 2029 -, ci sono tormenti quasi personali.

Tra i due, se fosse questione di rapporti personali, non ci sarebbe un millisecondo di dubbio: il feeling con Galliani, con cui parla la stessa lingua da anni, è epidermico, quasi primordiale. Quello con Malagò è al massimo il rapporto con un rivale che si rispetta, ma da cui lo dividono anni di battaglie rigorosamente l’uno da una parte e l’altro dall’altra. Il problema è che con Galliani ci sono calciatori e allenatori, che in primavera hanno rotto una storica alleanza con Abete per schierarsi… con Malagò, ponendo Giancarlo Viglione - il cui numero non è esattamente salvato tra i preferiti nella rubrica di Abete, mettiamola così - come pilastro di un accordo elettorale vissuto dal presidente della Lnd come un’imperdonabile fuga in avanti. Giancarlo Abete e Umberto Calcagno (presidente dell’Assocalciatori), nelle ultime settimane, si sono parlati più volte. Non si sono (ancora?) chiariti, di sicuro non si sono (ma lo faranno mai?) riappacificati, ma è forse quello il vero rapporto a cui guardare per capire come andranno queste elezioni così imprevedibili e purulente per la scia di veleni che si porteranno dietro anche quando finiranno.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

AC Milan put on a show for their fans at San Siro on Sunday evening as they beat Frosinone 5-1 to move back into the top four.

It was a game that promised entertainment from the early stages, and Milan took command thanks to an own-goal from Gabriele Calvani and a much-needed goal from Goncalo Ramos, before Patrizio Masini scored to halve the deficit.

It has been revealed that read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

The Rossoneri ran away with things in the second half, with Ardon Jashari and Alphadjo Cisse netting off the bench before Christian Pulisic got a goal of his own to add some gloss to the scoreline. There were chances to make it an even bigger margin, but five would have to do.

Given that Lazio, Roma, Como and Juventus had all won prior to kick-off, it was crucial that Milan matched their results to keep up the pressure at the top end of the table, and they did so in emphatic fashion.

In a recent development, ruben Amorim made just one change to the starting line-up from the side that won against Genoa before the break, with Alphadjo Cisse dropping out and Davide Bartesaghi coming in. It was uncertain from the line-up named what the system would be, as has often been the case with the Portuguese coach so far.

In a recent development, frosinone started the game better and called Mike Maignan into action inside the first minute with a close-range header that was saved, though the flag was up. Then, a deflected strike from Masini on the edge of the box ended up scraping the upright and going behind for a corner.

Sources indicate that however, it was Milan who struck first at San Siro. Luka Modric deserves the plaudits for an outstanding through ball to find Adrien Rabiot’s run in behind, and the Frenchman’s square pass was heading towards Christian Pulisic’s run but was turned into his own net by Calvani, leaving Palmisani rooted.

The frantic pace of the early stages continued, as a lovely exchange between Diego Moreira and Pulisic saw a threatening cross turned behind. A few minutes later, Yunus Musah found Moreira who had a shot deflected for a corner, which Goncalo Ramos rose and met well but headed over the bar.

Frosinone kept providing reminders that they too pose a threat going forward, such as on the quarter-hour mark when Kvernadze surged down the left and got off a low shot from a narrow angle that Maignan had to parry behind. The corner wasn’t properly dealt with, and Cittadini flashed one across the six-yard box that Rabiot had to put into the stands.

In a recent development, just like with the first goal, Milan punished Frosinone for not making the most of their spell of pressure. Goncalo Ramos was the man who started and finished a flowing counter-attack, robbing Calvani of possession before running towards goal. Musah’s through ball was run onto by the electric Moreira, who found Rabiot, and the Frenchman’s cut-back was tucked away by the Portuguese.

It has been revealed that the two-goal lead was very quickly halved though, as Frosinone got the goal their pressure had threatened. Kvernadze’s run down the left and cut-back from the byline was scuffed onwards by Ghedjemis into the path of Masini, who toe-poked it in at the far post.

In the 34th minute, there was a moment that enraged the Milan players, staff and fans. The referee blew his whistle for a shirt pull on Rabiot just as Milan went through on goal with two men in behind and just the goalkeeper to beat. The official apologised, but it felt like a certain goal had been taken away.

Sources indicate that it was a half played at a hundred miles an hour, and it ended that way too. Pulisic flashed an effort over the bar from a good position, while Davide Bartesaghi’s low cross towards Ramos was cut out in the nick of time as Milan continued to get joy down the flanks.

Sources indicate that amorim opted to make an intriguing change at half-time, bringing off Bartesaghi and replacing him with Ardon Jashari. This change in turn saw Musah shift to left-back, a role that he played against Genoa in the last match, and from minute one.

It has been revealed that the change proved to be an absolute masterstroke, as Jashari scored inside three minutes. A ball was sent long to Ramos who knocked it down to Rabiot, whose first touch was a lovely through ball to the Swiss midfield. It looked like he had overrun it with the square option not used, but he lashed a shot in at the near post.

Not long after the goal, Ramos gestured towards the bench that he felt some discomfort. He wanted to play through it but Amorim took no risks, opting to bring Alphadjo Cisse on to lead the line.

There was a rather rare occurrence in the 54th minute, as Milan were awarded an indirect free-kick after Palmisani picked up a back pass from Calvani. Modric laid it off to Rabiot, but the goalkeeper made up for his error with a good save.

Industry observers note that continuing the trend of impact substitutions, Cisse got his ninth goal of the season right on the hour mark. A Frosinone corner was cleared and Pulisic found Moreira who had the Italian for company, and he finished the through ball by the Belgian past Palmisani with his trademark composure. The offside flag went up, but after a long check the goal was given.

Milan continued to look like scoring every time they got out of their own half, and Pulisic joined the fun in the 68th minute with a goal of his own. Frosinone again left one man back for a corner that was cleared, allowing the American to easily outpace Terzic with a run from inside his own half, dinking over Palmisani to make it 5-1.

With 20 minutes left on the clock, Amorim brought Strahinja Pavlovic and Pervis Estupinan on for Diawara and Musah. The final change saw Omari Hutchinson replace Pulisic.

Recent findings suggest that pavlovic looked far from 100% when he came on, appearing dizzy at certain moments. The head coach seemed to suggest coming off so as not to risk things, but he played on.

According to recent reports, milan had chances to make the scoreline even more impressive, with Moreira and Hutchinson squandering a couple of chances on the break. However, at full-time the team were rightly applauded by the San Siro crowd.

Industry observers note that right, where were we? Three weeks on from the fifth round of Premier League fixtures in which the champions Arsenal were beaten 3-0 by Brighton and todays’ visitors, Leeds United, who remain unbeaten, drew in a tepid goalless fixture with Crystal Palace, we finally get to the sixth. As worrying as the result was at the Amex, Arsenal still created a shedload of chances and last season they were the one club that battered Leeds in both games – first early in the season when they were playing four at the back and before Dominic Calvert-Lewin, a late signing, was fully fit, and then later after they had successfully switched to a “base formation” of three centre-backs and the tactical flexibility that allowed.

Sources indicate that it was a 5-0 tanking in August and 4-0 in January, so to say Leeds travel to a ground at which they have never won more in hope than expectation would be as true as much as it is hackneyed. Adding to a sense of foreboding and thanks to Opta’s excellent Jonny Cooper, we also have to take into account the fact that Leeds, floodlight kings, have not won a Premier League match kicking off before 3pm since August 2022 and have not won a match in London since beating Brentford in May that year to save themselves from relegation. However, they do boast the division’s best defensive record – three goals conceded – and the No1 ranked goalkeeper in James Trafford who has a save percentage of 87. For all the sense of doom, though, Leeds have become a very good side and their spine – Trafford–Muharemovic–Ampadu–Calvert-Lewin marries steel and class.

Arsenall need no fanfare. Until the set-back in dear old Sussex by the sea, they had looked formidable most of the time and will have been champing at the bit to get back out there and prove it was an aberration. Mikel Arteta mentioned he has doubts about Declan Rice, Kai Havertz and Ezri Konsa but Ben White, Max Dowman and Chrsthian Mosquera are all available. For Leeds Joe Rodon is still out and Dan James was injured on international duty but Harry Wilson and Jean-Matteo Bahoya returned to training after knocks this week and Daniel Farke was relatively optimistic about their prospects.

#142574. Tech Report: Man United are in the relegation zone on merit and will need all of Mauricio Pochettino's coaching powers to get them out of it - they are chronically short of form and have forgotten how to win, writes CHRIS WHEELER

Tech Report: Man United are in the relegation zone on merit and will need all of Mauricio Pochettino's coaching powers to get them out of it - they are chronically short of form and have forgotten how to win, writes CHRIS WHEELER

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1074 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dailymail

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 02:00 EST, 23 November 2026 | Updated: 10:28 EST, 24 November 2026.
  • As the fourth goal flew in and Anfield rejoiced once again, Mauricio Pochettino stood on the touchline with his arms folded and turned to the Manchester United bench with an air of resignation.
  • In a recent development, what can he do to improve this shambles of a team?
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By CHRIS WHEELER, NORTHERN SPORTS WRITER.

Published: 02:00 EST, 23 November 2026 | Updated: 10:28 EST, 24 November 2026.

As the fourth goal flew in and Anfield rejoiced once again, Mauricio Pochettino stood on the touchline with his arms folded and turned to the Manchester United bench with an air of resignation.

In a recent development, what can he do to improve this shambles of a team? What could anyone do? United could change their head coach every game, but without the tools to do the job, the result will be largely the same.

Chief executive Omar Berrada stated in an interview during the week that United have improved since the summer, but who is he trying to kid? They are in the relegation zone on merit, and it will need all of Pochettino's coaching powers to get them out of it.

He emerged from the tunnel shortly before 4.30pm here dressed smartly in blue, and after greeting Andoni Iraola and his staff, spent a few moments gathering his thoughts while You'll Never Walk Alone echoed around Anfield.

According to recent reports, the game plan was in tatters inside 13 minutes, though, as he watched United go two goals and one man down. There was much finger wagging from Pochettino when Leny Yoro was somewhat harshly sent off, but the decision was never going to be overturned and nor should it be used to mask another United debacle.

As the enormity of the task he has taken on dawned upon him in the second half, the Liverpool fans taunted: 'Poch is the wheel.'.

Mauricio Pochettino's first game as Man United head coach ended in a 4-0 defeat at Liverpool.

The manner of the display was a microcosm of why United are mired in the relegation zone.

Pochettino made two changes to the line-up from Michael Carrick's last game in charge against Aston Villa, and the biggest of them backfired spectacularly.

Giving Matthijs de Ligt his Premier League start for more than a year against Liverpool at Anfield felt like a gamble as he replaced Harry Maguire in central defence.

'When I saw Matthijs de Ligt's name on the team-sheet I was absolutely stunned,' admitted former United defender Gary Neville on Sky Sports, citing De Ligt's performance on his only start since last November in the Champions League defeat by Como in October.

However, the Dutchman was at fault for misreading the situation that led to Yoro being sent off in the eighth minute for the foul on Alexander Isak that saw Dominik Szoboszlai fire Liverpool ahead from a free-kick, and was the nearest United defender to Florian Wirtz when he hooked in the second shortly afterwards.

De Ligt got away with falling flat on his face and allowing Isak a free run on goal just after the hour mark, but couldn't stop Bradley Barcola's cross going through his legs when Rio Ngumoha scored the third shortly afterwards.

The nightmare was complete when his ill-judged pass to Joshua Zirkzee let in Liverpool for Victor Munoz to make it 4-0.

Pochettino's other change was to leave out Amad Diallo - who has claimed a couple of memorable goals against Liverpool but hasn't scored for United in nearly a year - and play Patrick Dorgu on the left.

Dorgu returned from injury to head a dramatic late equaliser in Carrick's final game in charge, but he was deemed to be unfit for duty by Denmark who sent him home during the international break.

He started on the left side of attack but switched to left-back when Yoro was sent off and Pochettino reshuffled what is statistically the worst defence in Europe as he tried to avoid a bloodbath.

Matthijs de Ligt (right) endured a nightmare game at centre-back as United were thumped.

Pochettino's response to a horror start was to send on Maguire for Bryan Mbeumo, his best attacker, to provide extra protection for De Ligt.

Recent findings suggest that having started the game in United's familiar 4-2-3-1 formation, he switched to 5-3-1. Moving to a back-five when your team only has 10 men felt like damage limitation.

It needed some excellent saves from Senne Lammens - not to mention a crucial block by Maguire to send Isak's effort over the bar before half-time - to spare United from an embarrassing defeat on a par with the seven and five goal humiliations at the hands of Liverpool in recent years.

Even so, after seeing his team record a pitiful xG of 0.14 in a first half that saw United have one shot on target and four touches in the Liverpool box, he knew they had to pose more of an attacking threat if only to relieve the pressure on their defence.

Zirkzee replaced the anonymous Matheus Cunha at half-time in the hope that he could hold the ball up better, but the xG rose only marginally to 0.63 by the end compared to Liverpool's 4.38.

Pochettino sent on Mason Mount and Noussair Mazraoui for Youri Tielemans and Dorgu in the 65th minute, and they had only been on the pitch for a matter of seconds when Ngumoha got Liverpool's third.

Senne Lammens produced multiple save to prevent the scoreline from further embarrasment.

There are so many problems piled up for Pochettino, it will be difficult to know where to start when he returns to his desk at Carrington on Monday ahead of this week's Champions League tie against Sporting Lisbon in Portugal.

In a recent development, this is a team chronically short of form and confidence that has forgotten how to win. There are only so many changes he can make with the squad available until the January transfer window, so the Argentine is stuck with what he's got until then.

But United have simply got to stop giving up early goals. It was a problem that plagued Carrick against Atletico Madrid, Como, Roma and Villa, and any hope that Pochettino could stop the rot disappeared inside eight minutes here.

Yoro's red card was also United's fourth in the last eight games (and his second), which is another bad habit they will have to kick if Pochettino is going to turn this season from hell around.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Gerry Cardinale gave his thoughts after watching his AC Milan side run riot against Frosinone at San Siro this evening.

It has been yet another few days where the Milan owner has made his presence felt. After landing in Italy, he was at Milanello and Casa Milan on Saturday for a series of important meetings with the management and the squad, and then he watched first hand as the Rossoneri won tonight.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

An own-goal from Gabriele Calvani got the scoring going, before Goncalo Ramos, Ardon Jashari, Alphadjo Cisse and Christian Pulisic all scored in the 5-1 rout of Frosinone. It could have been more in truth, but it was another display of the level this team can play at.

Cardinale was interviewed by Michael Cuomo of TeleLombardia after the final whistle having made his way down from the stands, and his comments were relayed by MilanNews.

Industry observers note that how happy is he? Is he satisfied?

Industry observers note that “Well, I’m never satisfied, but the results speak for themselves. The boys were fantastic tonight. I hope you’re happy. I hope the fans are happy. I think the team is coming together really well.

“It’s a game, let’s keep it under control, but I’m really proud of the boys. This is a team. It’s a team that wants to win until the end.”.

Can you dream of winning the Scudetto?

Sources indicate that “Look, it’s November. We still have a long way to go. But we want to see improvements in every match. This weekend was very interesting if you look at the kind of results we’ve had. You can see that something is changing in Serie A.

According to recent reports, “I was very happy to see us not just win, but win by that margin. And so, we have to build on that, but as Amorim says, every match is something to build on, and we have a long way to go. I personally still expect us to compete for the Scudetto, but it’s a long way off. One match at a time.

“Now the focus is on the Europa League. Yes, and as Ruben said, we have to do both. European competitions are important. Everything is a test. If you want to win a Scudetto, you have to do it all the way, and that’s what we’ll do.”.

Could signings arrive in January?

Sources indicate that “Again: January is just another stage. As you know, the January transfer window is complicated. You have to be disciplined. You can’t just jump into something randomly. The only thing that will happen under my ownership is that every time we play in the transfer market, we’ll play to win.

“That’s the theme. That’s the theme I said at the beginning of this year. So, if we make a move in any transfer window, January or June, it will be a move that will count.”.

West Ham had hoped things would get better under Scott Parker, but the newly introduced boss is yet to oversee his first win since replacing Nuno Espirito Santo. Things got worse for Parker and WHUFC on Tuesday night as they lost 1-0 to Portsmouth, making it six Championship matches without a win to leave them down in 13th.

The Hammers are the league’s top scorers, and whilst Jarrod Bowen is leading the way with seven goals and seven assists, one surprise goal source has been Konstantinos Mavropanos on six. Strikers are struggling to step up, and Parker was a fresh lead talisman in January.

Sources indicate that on the flip side, the story is different for Mark Robins‘ Stoke City. After a tough start, the Potters look like one of the most complete teams in the Championship. After winning with 10 men against Birmingham City last week, City backed it up with a 2-1 win over Millwall, thanks to a George Hirst brace.

There’s a lot to like about Stoke City, but what really catches the eye is just how well they hold on to a lead. In their last five games, they have taken the lead on four occasions and not dropped a single point.

Recent findings suggest that “West Ham look a side made up of individuals rather than a team. That’s the problem that Scott Parker has to solve if he is to mould the Hammers into a side like his other previous promotion-winning outfits. Doing that against high-flying Stoke City does not look like the place to start.

In a recent development, “Mark Robins has his Potters team flying and looking good value for their 2nd-place position. Stoke City are so hard to score against, and if they take the lead, it’s almost game over. This team look the real deal and are only going in one direction.

Industry observers note that “WHUFC have the quality to win this game, but not the togetherness. It will all come down to who scores first, and Stoke usually do.”.

Industry observers note that “Most people would have thought West Ham would be the side sat in 2nd, while Stoke City languish in 13th. However, with 17 games of the season down, WHUFC are struggling for form, while the Potters just can’t stop winning.

“Given the talent on offer, it does feel like a matter of when the Hammers get going, rather than if. With his pedigree in the Championship and stars like Jarrod Bowen on the books, Scott Parker will find a winning formula. That remarked, four defeats in a six-game winless run is understandably worrying supporters.

According to recent reports, “The current situation at Stoke could not be much more different. They are absolutely up on cloud nine at the moment, with five Championship wins on the trot lifting them into 2nd. The numbers might suggest a dip in form is coming, but when you’re tight at the back and have goals coming from multiple sources, you’re going to win games.

“The London Stadium is not a happy place at the moment, and with SCFC coming into the game in such confidence, you have to think the visitors win again with more misery ahead for Parker and co.”.

Watch out, AlphaFold: Claude and ChatGPT’s newly introduced biology skills wow scientists

📅 27 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (949 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nature

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Accurately predicting protein structures has been the preserve of specialist AI tools like AlphaFold — but now general-purpose models are catching up.
  • Recent findings suggest that earlier this month, Xinming Tu set out to test what artificial-intelligence models know about proteins.
  • He left the analysis to run overnight and woke up shocked at the results.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Accurately predicting protein structures has been the preserve of specialist AI tools like AlphaFold — but now general-purpose models are catching up. Credit: EMBL-EBI (CC0).

Recent findings suggest that earlier this month, Xinming Tu set out to test what artificial-intelligence models know about proteins. Tu, a researcher at an AI biology firm called Phylo in South San Francisco, California, asked large language models (LLMs) from OpenAI, Anthropic and Google to predict the sequences of obscure bacterial proteins.

He left the analysis to run overnight and woke up shocked at the results. The latest versions of Anthropic’s Claude models had outperformed other LLMs — but also specialized ‘protein language models’, which are trained on vast troves of sequence data and specially designed for such tasks.

Scientists are using AI to dream up revolutionary new proteins.

Scientists are using AI to dream up revolutionary new proteins.

When Tu and Leo Chen, a computational biologist at Harvard Medical School in Boston, Massachusetts, shared the results in a 16 November blogpost, it set off a frenzy among computational biologists to see what other protein biology LLMs such as Claude could do. For instance, Tu and Chen and others have found it could perform a key step in protein-structure prediction.

Sources indicate that and on 24 November, OpenAI announced that its latest language models had successfully designed latest proteins, some of which behaved as expected when made and tested in the lab. The results hint that the latest LLMs might be gaining a sophisticated understanding of protein biology.

Sources indicate that the research has kicked off a debate over the future of biological AI. Some scientists predict that ‘general purpose’ models such as Claude and ChatGPT will eventually outperform specialist tools such as AlphaFold at tasks including protein structure prediction and design.

“We want to see a world where a scientist can just describe in natural language what they want a ChatGPT model to do, and the model can just be infinitely flexible and design exactly what the person wants,” notes Joy Jiao, who leads life-sciences research at OpenAI in San Francisco, California.

But some researchers question the extent to which LLMs are learning underlying lessons in protein biology. They suggest that some of their abilities could be the result of regurgitating training data.

In a recent development, the release of AlphaFold2, Google DeepMind’s blockbuster protein-structure-prediction AI, in 2020 released a revolution in biological AI. There is now a vast ecosystem of software — much of it open source — for modelling different properties of proteins, such as how they interact with possible drugs, and for designing latest proteins.

It has been revealed that researchers have begun using LLMs to orchestrate these specialist models, but it has mostly been as a time-saving measure, says Martin Pačesa, a structural biologist at the University of Zurich. “In most cases, a specialist will always perform better than a generalist for a given task,” he says.

Five protein-design questions that still challenge AI.

Five protein-design questions that still challenge AI.

According to recent reports, to see if an LLM could stand in for specialist protein-design tools, Jiao and her colleagues asked an OpenAI model called GPT-6.2 to design 3D protein structures capable of binding to five different biological targets, including proteins implicated in cancer and immune disorders. After the LLMs generated the designs, the researchers used a specialist AI tool to determine a corresponding genetic sequence. Lab experiments confirmed that around 11% of designs were able to bind their target.

Sources indicate that in other experiments, the OpenAI team indicated that its LLMs could design protein sequences, redesign existing antibodies, and other tasks typically performed by specialist tools. In some cases, the LLM performed as well as some specialist tools, and in others, such as predicting the 3D structure of proteins, it was far off. OpenAI researchers describe the work in a blogpost and technical paper.

Jiao emphasizes that the work is a proof of principle, and that specialized AI tools were still needed for key steps. But Masatoshi Uehara, an OpenAI researcher who was part of the effort, believes that LLMs will only get better at protein biology. “I believe the large language model can technically beat every specialized model in even each capability,” he says.

doi: https://doi.org/10.1038/d41586-026-03836-z.

Man Utd make worst start in 40 years after being hauled back by 10-man Spurs
